newsitem.title: CHINA: China's '97 crude imports seen rising to 30 mln T.
newsitem.headline: China's '97 crude imports seen rising to 30 mln T.

text.p: China is expected to import over 30 million tonnes of crude oil in 1997, up from 22.6 million tonnes last year, a senior official of China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) said on Wednesday.
Imports could rise to 40 million tonnes in the year 2000, Zeng Xingqiu, CNPC vice president, told Reuters.
He linked the expected rise to growing demand from a rapidly expanding domestic economy, adding that this outpaced increases in production.
China's crude output from two main onshore oilfields, Daqing and Shengli, has been stagnating in recent years.
Daqing currently produces around 50 million tonnes per year and Shengli about 30 million tonnes.
CNPC hopes to stabilise production at Daqing and wants to boost output at Shengli to 40 million tonnes.
Refiners are also likely to rely more on imported crude as China deregulates its oil industry and allows domestic crude oil prices to rise, other oil industry officials said.
